issues.legal_issue: A second appellate court may not disturb concurrent factual findings by reassessing the evidence without a substantial question of law.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court made concurrent findings on the parties’ agreement, readiness and willingness, and the alleged later agreement and payment.
The High Court reversed findings on mixed questions of law and fact without discussing the evidence and without framing a substantial question of law.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s interference exceeded the jurisdiction available in a second appeal and was unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended in 1976, the High Court’s jurisdiction in a second appeal is confined to substantial questions of law; Section 100(5) contemplates framing such a question. Interference with factual findings requiring reappreciation of evidence is not warranted, as held in Panchugopal Barua v. Umesh Chandra Goswami, 1997 (4) SCC 713, and Kshitish Chandra Purkait v. Santosh Kumar Purkait, 1997 (5) SCC 438.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_fact_findings and no_substantial_law_question_framed and high_court_reassessed_evidence

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding was a second appeal from decisions of the trial court and first appellate court.
predicates.concurrent_fact_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual findings.
predicates.no_substantial_law_question_framed: The High Court did not frame a substantial question of law for decision.
predicates.high_court_reassessed_evidence: The High Court disturbed factual findings by reassessing or drawing conclusions from the evidence.

issues.definition: When a second appeal involves concurrent factual findings and the High Court reassesses the evidence without framing a substantial question of law, its interference is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking specific performance must prove readiness and willingness to perform the essential contractual obligations.
material_facts: The agreement required the purchaser to complete the purchase within a stipulated period that the lower courts found was essential.
The purchaser made no effective effort to complete the purchase during that period and brought the specific-performance suit years after it expired.
The purchaser falsely claimed to have made a payment under an alleged later agreement and relied on a document found to be fabricated.
The lower courts found that the purchaser had not been ready and willing to perform the contract.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser failed to establish readiness and willingness, so the decree for specific performance could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires a plaintiff seeking specific performance to aver and prove performance, or continuous readiness and willingness to perform, the essential terms required of that plaintiff. A false claim of payment supported by a fabricated document is inconsistent with readiness and willingness to perform the contractual payment obligation.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding was a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.plaintiff_failed_to_prove_readiness: The plaintiff did not establish readiness and willingness to perform the essential contractual obligations.
predicates.false_payment_claim: The plaintiff falsely asserted that a payment had been made and relied on a fabricated document to support that assertion.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, a plaintiff who fails to prove readiness and willingness and falsely claims to have made a contractual payment cannot obtain specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: A plea for protection based on part performance cannot succeed when it is raised for the first time in second appeal without a foundation in the pleadings or when the claimant has not shown willingness to perform the contract.
material_facts: The purchaser raised the part-performance plea for the first time in second appeal, without a foundation in the pleadings and without having raised it in either lower court.
The purchaser had failed to prove willingness to perform the contract.
issues.conclusion: The part-performance plea could not be entertained in second appeal, and the purchaser was not entitled to protection of possession on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act raises a mixed question of law and fact and cannot be urged for the first time at the second-appeal stage without a foundation in the pleadings. Willingness to perform the claimant’s part of the contract is also an essential ingredient of the part-performance plea.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding was a second appeal.
predicates.part_performance_plea_first_raised_witho: The claimant raised a part-performance plea for the first time in second appeal without a foundation in the pleadings.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_show_contractual_will: The claimant did not establish willingness to perform the claimant’s part of the contract.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, part-performance protection is unavailable when the plea is first raised without a pleading foundation or the claimant has failed to show contractual willingness.

issues.legal_issue: Execution of a decree during the appeal does not extinguish the judgment debtor’s right to pursue the appeal absent waiver or conscious abandonment.
material_facts: The decree under appeal was executed and a sale deed was made through court intervention before a stay was obtained.
The judgment debtor had already sought appellate review and there was no showing that the judgment debtor waived or consciously abandoned the appeal.
issues.conclusion: Execution of the decree did not deprive the judgment debtor of the right to prosecute the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment debtor’s appellate right is not lost merely because the decree was executed before a stay order, unless there is something to show that the judgment debtor waived or consciously gave up that right.

predicates.appeal_from_decree: The proceeding was an appeal by a judgment debtor against a decree.
predicates.decree_executed_before_stay: The decree was executed before a stay order prevented its execution.
predicates.no_waiver_or_abandonment: There was no showing that the judgment debtor waived or consciously abandoned the appeal.

issues.definition: When a judgment debtor appeals a decree that is executed before a stay, the appeal survives if the judgment debtor did not waive or consciously abandon it.
